title.en: The Habait look, Tel Aviv luxury v1
title.fr: Le look Habait, luxe Tel Aviv v1

ruling: D-WQ-22 (2026-10-28): one Habait designer look on every new-build walk, swappable per project; the board is the single source of the skin's material words, so every room is skinned from the same sentences

surfaces.floor: large-format pale limestone-look porcelain floor tiles (120 by 120 cm, matte, light sand, thin grout lines) — Image 1 already draws this floor’s grout grid at its true places and spacing: keep every grout line exactly where it is, make the tiles follow that grid, and draw no other floor pattern
surfaces.ceiling: flat warm white ceiling with slim recessed spots and a linear warm LED cove
surfaces.feature: a micro-cement feature wall in warm greige behind the TV (no slatted panel, no wood)
surfaces.doors: zero-line interior doors: full-height, frameless, flush with the wall, concealed hinges, no architrave, no panels, painted the wall colour, a slim matte black lever
surfaces.kitchen: a bulthaup b3 kitchen: handleless fronts in matte sand-grey lacquer with a continuous recessed horizontal grip channel in brushed aluminium, a very thin (12 mm) brushed stainless-steel worktop with a flush integrated sink and a slim stainless tap, a brushed stainless-steel function-wall splashback with one long horizontal rail and two slim open shelves, a flush black induction hob under a ceiling-flush extractor, the fridge and ovens fully integrated behind flush fronts; no visible handles, no framed or panelled fronts, no wood-grain or brown fronts, no stone splashback
surfaces.bathrooms: large pale stone-look tiles, a floating handleless vanity in matte sand-grey lacquer, a round backlit mirror, matte black fittings, a frameless glass shower screen (the floor’s grout grid is drawn in Image 1 at its true places: keep every grout line where it is)
surfaces.wardrobe: floor-to-ceiling handleless wardrobe fronts in matte sand-grey lacquer, flush, recessed grip channels, no panels, no frames, no wood-grain
surfaces.glazing: slim black-framed floor-to-ceiling glazing; the terrace railing is frameless clear glass with a slim black handrail
surfaces.terrace: pale porcelain terrace tiles, a built-in planter with olive trees, a lounger and a low table (the floor’s grout grid is drawn in Image 1 at its true places: keep every grout line where it is)

textiles: ivory and sand textiles, linen curtains, a wool rug, a few books and a plant
light: soft bright morning daylight from the glass facade, realistic shadows and reflections
windows: Through every window and glass wall: floor 16 of a high-rise - a bright, hazy, slightly overexposed sky and, far below, a soft, out-of-focus, unrecognisable pale city haze; no landmark, no sea, no specific building, no street detail.
avoid: Avoid: text, labels, watermarks, people, pets, mirrored or duplicated rooms, borders, panels, a fisheye circle, black corners, a visible seam, any change to the position or size of a wall, an opening or a piece of furniture. No glass doors or glass partitions between rooms of the apartment (interior doors are zero-line flush doors or open doorways); no balcony, railing or terrace invented behind a window; no window, door or glass wall added where the list of openings names none. No wood-grain or brown cabinet fronts, no framed or panelled doors or fronts, no visible handles on cabinetry, no slatted wood panels.

dressing.living: an ivory linen sofa with sand cushions, a round travertine coffee table, a wool rug, the TV on the micro-cement feature wall, a floor lamp, plants, books
dressing.kitchen: the counter dressed with a bowl of fruit, a kettle, a few books; the dining table set with simple ceramics
dressing.hall: a slim console with a round mirror, a coat niche, a runner
dressing.bedroom: a bed with ivory linen, floating bedside tables in matte sand-grey lacquer with small lamps, a handleless dresser, linen curtains
dressing.bathroom: folded towels, a plant, a wooden stool
dressing.storage: the wardrobe fronts closed, a bench, a runner
dressing.balcony: a lounger, a low table, planters with olive trees

outdoor_line: THIS IS AN OUTDOOR SPACE: a covered terrace on floor 16, open air beyond its glass railing, the deck above as its ceiling, the apartment's glass facade on the other side with the rooms visible through the glass; keep the railing, the sky and the hazy city exactly where the render shows them; no interior walls, no sofa, no TV, no kitchen on the terrace: only terrace furniture (a lounger, a low table, planters with olive trees) on pale porcelain terrace tiles.

fixture_words.counter: a fitted bulthaup-style kitchen run: handleless matte sand-grey lacquer fronts with a recessed grip channel, a 12 mm brushed stainless-steel worktop, a flush integrated stainless sink with a slim stainless tap, a stainless function-wall splashback with a long rail
fixture_words.tall_unit: a tall handleless matte sand-grey lacquer column with the oven and the fridge fully integrated behind flush fronts
fixture_words.tall_unit_fridge: a tall column that IS the panel-ready integrated fridge-freezer, hidden behind the SAME handleless matte sand-grey lacquer fronts as the kitchen run (the same colour, the same recessed grip channel): two flush full-height doors (a tall fridge door above a freezer door); no stainless-steel, chrome or metal doors, no visible appliance face, no oven, no microwave and no open niche in this column (the oven is built in under the hob); the grey block in the render is only its placeholder
fixture_words.tall_unit_oven: a tall handleless matte sand-grey lacquer oven column: the built-in oven and a compact oven stacked at eye height behind flush black glass, flush lacquer fronts above and below them
fixture_words.tall_unit_pantry: a tall handleless matte sand-grey lacquer storage column with flush full-height doors and the recessed grip channel; no appliance in it
fixture_words.island: a bulthaup-style kitchen island: a thin brushed stainless-steel top on handleless matte sand-grey lacquer fronts, two stools
fixture_words.sofa: an ivory linen sofa with sand cushions
fixture_words.tv_unit: a low handleless TV unit in matte sand-grey lacquer, the TV on the micro-cement feature wall above it
fixture_words.bed: a bed with ivory linen and a low upholstered headboard
fixture_words.bedside: a floating bedside table in matte sand-grey lacquer with a small lamp
fixture_words.wardrobe: floor-to-ceiling handleless wardrobe fronts in matte sand-grey lacquer, flush, recessed grip channels, no panels, no frames, no wood-grain
fixture_words.vanity: a floating handleless vanity in matte sand-grey lacquer with a stone basin and a round backlit mirror above it
fixture_words.shower: a walk-in shower on a pale stone tray behind a frameless glass screen
fixture_words.lounger: a teak lounger with an ivory cushion

fixtures_line_head: The plain light-grey blocks in Image 1 are furniture placeholders, each at its true place and size: dress each one as what it is, keep its footprint and height, and add no other large piece of furniture.
skin_prompt_template: Image 1 is a plain computer render of the {ROOM_EN} ({ROOM_HE}) of a real apartment: a 360-degree equirectangular panorama (2:1; its left and right edges meet behind the camera). {OUTDOOR_LINE}{ANCHOR_LINE} {NEIGHBOURS} {FIXTURES} Re-render Image 1 as a photograph of the same room: keep every wall, window, door, opening, column, ceiling height and every piece of furniture exactly where it is and exactly the same size; do not add, remove or move any opening, wall, cabinet run or island; keep the camera position and the equirectangular projection unchanged, with the left and right edges joining seamlessly and the zenith and nadir continuous. Replace only the materials and the dressing with this look: {FLOOR}; {WALLS}; {CEILING}; {FEATURE}; {DOORS}; {ROOM_SURFACES}; {GLAZING}; {TEXTILES}. Dressing for this room, small and in place: {DRESSING}. {LIGHT}. {WINDOWS} Photoreal materials, natural shadows and reflections, no text, no people, no watermark. {AVOID}

anchor_lines.first: This is the first room skinned: it defines the apartment's look, and every other room will be matched to it.
anchor_lines.next: Image 2 is the finished {ANCHOR_ROOM} of the SAME apartment, already rendered as a photograph: it fixes the materials of this home (the same floor, walls, glazing, fronts, counters, ceiling light, curtains, daylight and city haze); match it piece for piece. Image 3 is a second reference of the same look.

draft.use: drafts and my review; the apartment anchor for the next draft

final.use: the finals; the living room first, then every room against it

reserve.use: a stricter, more literal skin when GPT moves a piece

evidence: qa-evidence/tour360/walkaround-quality/probes/PROBES.md P03, P04 (2026-10-28): GPT Image 2.5 and Muse kept every wall and opening of the pilot apartment's CG render; a second room skinned against the first came back as the same apartment
changes: 1.1.0 (2026-10-28 night): the outdoor line for terrace cameras; the per-view list of what every opening is, built from the plan by make-skin-prompts.mjs ({NEIGHBOURS}); the avoid list forbids interior glass doors, invented balconies and unlisted openings — after the first Muse drafts drew a corridor behind the main bedroom's glass, a balcony behind bedroom 2's window and glass doors in the wardrobe

1.2.0 (2026-10-29, OQ-2 / D-WQ-33 step 3): the floor sentences tell the model that Image 1 already carries the real grout grid (the CG scene now draws the tile grid, pipeline v1.4.0) and to keep every grout line where it is — after the eleven finals drew every grout line freehand in equirect space and the lines came out bent in the viewer

1.3.0 (2026-11-01, Eliran): the look moved to the current line — a bulthaup b3 kitchen (handleless matte sand-grey lacquer, a thin stainless worktop, a stainless function wall), zero-line doors (frameless, flush, no architrave, no panels), handleless matte-lacquer wardrobes and vanities, a micro-cement feature wall instead of the slatted oak panel; no brown or wood-grain fronts anywhere
